telos.statement: Develop the most useful architecture-expertise capability for the peer-agent system without building more machinery than the current state justifies.
telos.success_condition: The next architecture-agent decision is better bounded, cheaper to reverse, and supported by evidence about which resources materially improve it.

current_state.summary: Neta and the R&D Agent exist as peers under a shared epistemic kernel. R&D v0.1 is retained as a frozen comparator; R&D v0.2 resource↔telos calibration is an unvalidated candidate used by this loop. No architecture expert agent or learned orchestrator exists yet.
known_constraints: Do not create implicit hierarchy between peers.
Do not promote OSS patterns merely because successful systems use them.
Do not build an orchestrator before routing failures justify it.
Treat scaffold and same-model peer agreement as candidate reasoning, not independent empirical triangulation.

decision_blocked.statement: What is the smallest evidence-backed Architecture Agent capability and evaluation contract worth building next?
decision_blocked.current_default: Do not build the Architecture Agent until the missing architectural judgments and their tests are discriminated.
decision_blocked.reversal_condition: A bounded analysis identifies decision-relevant architecture judgments that are not already supplied more cheaply by existing resources and defines falsifiable tests for them.

signals: Architecture expertise is the next desired peer capability.
The owner wants R&D, Neta and an external reasoning scaffold to learn from one another while preserving distinct roles.
